kill_fact: The kill attempt fails on the catalyst but lands on the file's cash arithmetic. Every load-bearing deal term checks out against the primary record: the executed 5 Feb 2026 Share Purchase Agreement (filed in full as an exhibit to the 10 Mar 2026 6-K) pays US$717 million with no financing condition, permits a pre-closing withdrawal of up to US$280 million, carries tiered termination fees of US$150m / US$75m on the buyer and US$75m on the company, and is gated on SAMR anti-monopoly clearance inside a 12-month Longstop Date (about 5 Feb 2027, extendable in writing). Both AGM resolutions - approval of the Transaction AND authority to deploy not less than 90% of post-closing cash - were adopted 27 Mar 2026. The event has NOT fired, slipped or been priced: the issuer's last word on it (Q1 release, 21 May 2026) is that the deal 'has not been completed, and is subject to ... receipt of anti-monopoly clearance from the SAMR', no SEC filing of any kind has followed after 26 May 2026, and the shares still trade at $2.39 against a gross ceiling of about $4.60. What does NOT survive is the claim that the US$150m retention test is 'comfortably satisfied' with 'roughly US$290 million of headroom.' The test is not run on the RMB3.14bn Cayman CONSOLIDATED figure the file cites, but on Dingdong BVI's consolidated net cash as of 31 Dec 2025 minus the amounts withdrawn, and the 10 Feb 2026 announcement is explicit that any shortfall lets the Buyer cut the purchase price. Per the Q1 balance sheet, only RMB45.7 million sat outside the held-for-sale China group at the base date, so BVI net cash was about RMB3,094.6m (about US$442m): after the full US$280m draw the cushion above the US$150m floor is roughly US$12m, about 3%, and it is set by a Big Four closing audit under the SPA's own broader Net Cash definition, not by the press-release number. The US$997m is therefore a ceiling with a thin margin, and the withdrawal and the price are coupled, not additive-and-free. Second correction, to the floor: about 99% of the cited 'hard backing' net cash (RMB3,094.6m of RMB3,140.3m) sits INSIDE the entity being sold; the parent held RMB45.7m at 31 Dec 2025 and about US$54m at 31 Mar 2026, roughly $0.25 per ADS. In the break branch holders do not own a distributable cash pile - they own a Chinese operating company whose cash is working capital, still behind the same discretionary board and the same FX approvals. And the US$75m fee is payable only on termination at/after a Longstop Date the parties may extend by mutual consent, so it backstops no particular date. The asymmetry survives - live, binding, unfired, wide spread - but it is thinner and later-dated than the file's floor implies.
corrections:
1) MATERIAL - the retention test. The file (bull_thesis, sop_bull, sop_breakdown, interrogator_dossier sec.2) states the US$150m floor is 'comfortably satisfied' against reported net cash of RMB3.14bn 'so the full withdrawal is collectable without reducing the headline price', with 'roughly $290 million of headroom'. Wrong entity. Per the 10 Feb 2026 6-K the test is 'the total net cash of Dingdong BVI and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis as of December 31, 2025 minus such amounts received by Dingdong Cayman shall not be less than US$150 million', and SPA Art. 2.3(4) gives the Investor the right to reduce the Equity Transfer Price by any shortfall, as determined by a jointly appointed Big Four closing auditor. The Q1 2026 balance sheet shows only RMB45,722k of cash outside the held-for-sale China group at 31 Dec 2025, so BVI net cash was about RMB3,094.6m (about US$442m at the Q4 conversion rate). Cushion after a full US$280m draw: about US$12m (about 3%), not US$290m. Any audit adjustment beyond that cuts the price dollar-for-dollar. Keep US$997m / $4.60 gross as a CEILING; do not carry it as the collectable base case.
2) MINOR - citation. The 'up to US$997 million' phrase is the company's, but it comes from the 10 February 2026 announcement (Dingdong Announces Intention to Utilize Substantial Majority of Proceeds), NOT from the fourth-quarter release of 4/5 March 2026 as bull_thesis, sop_bull and the dossier state. The Q4 release contains no such figure - it mentions only the 5 Feb and 10 Feb announcements.
3) MATERIAL for dating - the 31 August 2026 withdrawal date is NOT unverified. dated_milestone and forcing_function carry it as 'could not be re-verified from a primary document'. It is in the 10 February 2026 6-K verbatim ('Dingdong Cayman will have the right to receive prior to August 31, 2026 total cash not exceeding US$280 million') and in SPA Art. 6.17 filed with the 10 Mar 2026 6-K. But Art. 6.17 adds 'or within an appropriately extended period, provided it does not affect the Closing Auditor's ability to issue the agreed-upon procedures report prior to the Satisfaction Date' - so it is a soft checkpoint, not a forcing date. Upgrade it to verified AND label it non-binding; passing 31 Aug 2026 with no withdrawal is not evidence of failure.
4) MATERIAL for the floor's composition - sop_bear and moderator_conclusion present '$2.03 a share of company-reported net cash' as hard backing. That cash is almost entirely inside Dingdong BVI (RMB3,094.6m of RMB3,140.3m at 31 Dec 2025); parent-level liquidity was RMB45.7m at the base date and about US$54m (cash RMB212.0m + short-term investments RMB159.1m) at 31 Mar 2026, i.e. about $0.25 per ADS. In a broken deal the cash is not distributable proceeds, it is a Chinese operating company's working capital, subject to the same board discretion and FX approvals the file identifies as the central risk. The 18% haircut to $1.95 is defensible in direction but is doing more work than the text admits.
5) MINOR - the US$75m clearance-failure fee. SPA Art. 8.3(c)(iii) pays it only if the Anti-monopoly Review 'fails to be passed/completed by the Longstop Date' AND the agreement is terminated or rescinded. Art. 8.2(a) lets the parties extend the Longstop Date in writing. A mutual extension means no termination, no fee, and more waiting - so the $0.35 is not a backstop at any date the file underwrites to.
6) MINOR - confirmations, not corrections: the SPA's Art. 2.4 does state that all profits and losses of the Group Companies from the 31 Dec 2025 Base Date to Closing 'shall be enjoyed or born by the Transferee', which validates the file's central 'the earnings are already the buyer's' insight; the held-for-sale D&A add-back of RMB138m against RMB165.4m of net income, the overseas loss of RMB71.4m on RMB139.4m of revenue, and the tiered fee structure are all verbatim-correct. AGM Resolution 2's operative words are 'in its absolute discretion', which is stronger support for the bear's governance point than the file's paraphrase.
evidence: Dingdong (Cayman) Ltd, Form 6-K filed 5 Feb 2026 (SEC accession 0001193125-26-038494), Ex-99.1 'Dingdong Announces Entry into Definitive Agreement to Sell its China Business to Meituan': 'after Dingdong (Cayman) Limited receives total cash not exceeding US$280 million from Dingdong BVI and its subsidiaries (provided that the remaining net cash ... shall not be less than US$150 million), the Buyer will pay total cash consideration of US$717 million ... subject to adjustments based on certain net cash, net working capital and other financial line items'; tiered fees US$150m (buyer fails to close), US$75m (buyer, if anti-monopoly or other clearance cannot be obtained despite the Company's cooperation), US$75m (company); 'may be terminated if closing does not occur within 12 months, which may be extended with mutual consent'; closing conditions = shareholder approval, SAMR anti-monopoly clearance, overseas carve-out, non-resident indirect transfer tax filings, no MAE; five-year Greater China non-compete by Company and Founder; 90/10 payment split with the 10% released after taxes are settled.

Form 6-K filed 10 Feb 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-043759), Ex-99.1: 'Dingdong Cayman will have the right to receive prior to August 31, 2026 total cash not exceeding US$280 million from Dingdong BVI and its subsidiaries (provided that the total net cash of Dingdong BVI and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis as of December 31, 2025 minus such amounts received by Dingdong Cayman shall not be less than US$150 million). As such, Dingdong Cayman expects that it will receive up to US$997 million in cash proceeds ... In the event that the net cash of Dingdong BVI and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis as of December 31, 2025 minus the amounts received by Dingdong Cayman as described above is less than US$150 million, the Buyer has the right to adjust the purchase price cash consideration at closing for any such shortfalls.' Same release: the 90% capital-return language is an intention whose terms 'will be determined after the closing ... and subject to approval by the Company's Board of Directors', with 'no assurance'.

Form 6-K filed 10 Mar 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-099399), Ex-99.2 Notice of 2026 AGM with the full Share Purchase Agreement of 5 Feb 2026 attached - Resolution 1 approval of the Transaction; Resolution 2 authorising the Board 'to utilize not less than 90% of the Company's cash balance after the closing ... at such time, in such manner as the Board, in its absolute discretion, deems appropriate'; SPA Art. 2.3(4) (price reduction if BVI Base-Date Net Cash minus withdrawals is under US$150m, per Big Four closing auditor); Art. 2.4 (all Base-Date-to-Closing profits and losses accrue to the Transferee); Art. 6.17 Fund Withdrawal Arrangements ('no later than August 31, 2026 (or within an appropriately extended period ...)'); Art. 8.2(a) Longstop Date = 12 months after the 5 Feb 2026 Signing Date 'or such longer period as otherwise agreed in writing'; Art. 8.3(c)(iii) buyer's US$75m fee only where the Anti-monopoly Review is not passed by the Longstop Date and the agreement is terminated. All resolutions adopted at the AGM held 27 Mar 2026 (6-K, accession 0001193125-26-127836).

Form 6-K filed 22 May 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-235450), Q1 2026 results dated 21 May 2026: 'As of the date of this release, the transaction has not been completed, and is subject to ... the receipt of anti-monopoly clearance from the SAMR'; consolidated net cash after short-term borrowings RMB3,140.3m at 31 Dec 2025 and RMB3,210.6m at 31 Mar 2026; continuing-operations (non-China) balance sheet shows cash of only RMB45,722k at 31 Dec 2025 and RMB212,045k plus RMB159,146k of short-term investments (about US$54m) at 31 Mar 2026; overseas net loss RMB71.4m on revenue RMB139.4m; held-for-sale suspension of D&A added about RMB138m to RMB165.4m of net income. Verified 28 Jul 2026: EDGAR shows NO Dingdong filing of any type after the Form 3 of 26 May 2026, no clearance or closing announcement, and DDL last traded at $2.39 (market cap $517.6m) - the catalyst is live and unfired, about six months into a twelve-month window.
